Women's World Cup 2027 host cities map

By Olive · Updated 2026-11-25

The 2027 Women's World Cup, played from 24 June to 25 July 2027, is spread across eight Brazilian cities, from Fortaleza, less than 4° south of the equator, to Porto Alegre in the far south. The map shows where each one sits, coloured by region.

Host cities at a glance

CityStadiumRegionHosts up toStraight-line distance from Rio
Rio de JaneiroEstádio do MaracanãSouth-eastFinal—
São PauloArena ItaqueraSouth-eastSemi-final, third-place matchabout 360 km

BrasíliaEstádio NacionalCentral-WestRound of 16about 930 km
SalvadorArena Fonte NovaNorth-eastRound of 16about 1,210 km
RecifeArena de PernambucoNorth-eastRound of 16about 1,880 km
Porto AlegreEstádio Beira-RioSouthRound of 16about 1,120 km

Straight-line (great-circle) distances are measured between the city coordinates listed on Wikipedia, rounded to the nearest 10 km. Road and flight distances are longer.

Reading the map

  • The south-east cluster of Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo and Belo Horizonte is the closest group: Rio is about 360 km from São Paulo and about 340 km from Belo Horizonte, and São Paulo and Belo Horizonte are about 490 km apart.
  • The north-east cities of Fortaleza, Recife and Salvador lie along the Atlantic coast, more than 1,000 km from Rio.
  • Brasília is inland, in the Brazilian Highlands of the Central-West region. Porto Alegre is far to the south: about 350 km in a straight line from Jaguarão on the Uruguayan border, against about 1,120 km from Rio.

For travel between regions, see getting between host cities. Each city also has its own guide, linked in the table.
